reason: Selected abstract, scope and model-free probe sections support testing side-effect barrier semantics. Full repair proof and deployment contract were not reviewed.

candidates.title: Probe cancellation and approval at the side-effect boundary
candidates.rule: Before relying on an agent framework approval, cancellation or timeout control, test whether parallel, replayed or already-running tools can still commit effects after the control fires.
candidates.finding: Model-free witness workflows separate sibling leakage, replay duplication, cancellation orphans and timeout zombies. These are distinct framework behaviors; the recommendation is to reproduce relevant probes for the deployed versions.
models: Model-free control-flow probes; live-model reachability is separate
workloads: Six pinned open-source agent runtimes spanning Python and JavaScript
candidates.conditions: Effects must be observed at the actual commit boundary. Five frameworks have pre-execution gates; the post-hoc-only framework is not a sixth approval-gate violation.
candidates.limitations: The inspected paper contains inconsistent four-versus-five wording in a footnote. Version-specific results are not a claim that every axis fails in every framework or in current releases. Complete mediation is a prerequisite for the proposed repair; proof details were not reviewed.
candidates.validation_test: Use disposable effects to test pause/reject with parallel siblings, approval resume, cancellation during blocking work and timeout during in-flight work. Assert event order and exactly-once behavior for the deployed runtime.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
